subject: Anthropology
title: The Moral Economy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Moral Economy.

hook.text: Peasants revolt not when they're poor but when the rules of fairness are broken. Economics has a moral dimension.

buildup.text: James Scott argued that traditional economies follow moral norms — guaranteeing subsistence before extracting surplus.

discovery.text: The moral economy is the set of shared expectations about fairness that regulate economic life in communities.

twist.text: Capitalism disrupts moral economies. When profit replaces fairness, communities lose their economic safety net.

climax.text: Moral economies show that fairness isn't a luxury. It's the foundation on which stable economic life depends.

quiz.question: What is a moral economy?
options: An economy based on profit alone
Shared expectations about fairness that regulate economic life

details.summary: The moral economy concept, developed by E. P. Thompson and James Scott, describes how communities enforce norms of fairness, reciprocity, and subsistence security that constrain market behavior. When these moral expectations are violated, protest and resistance follow.
details.whyItMatters: The moral economy reveals that economic life always operates within a framework of moral expectations. Market disruptions cause resistance not because people fear change but because they experience violations of deeply held norms of fairness and.
takeaways: Moral economy describes community norms that constrain market behavior
Norms of fairness and subsistence security govern economic expectations
Violation of moral economy norms triggers protest and resistance

faq.question: What is E. P. Thompson's concept of moral economy?
faq.answer: Thompson argued that 18th-century English food riots were not mindless mob behavior but disciplined responses to violations of customary norms about fair prices and bread availability. Crowds enforced a moral economy that markets were expected to respect.

faq.question: How did James Scott apply moral economy to peasant societies?
faq.answer: Scott showed that Southeast Asian peasants resisted not when they were poor — they were always poor — but when landlords and states violated the subsistence ethic guaranteeing minimum survival. Moral economy resistance defends the right to subsistence against market and state extraction.
